narrative.overview: Tikvah pairs the composure of an editorial reading experience with the reassurance of a carefully prepared support space. Warm paper surfaces, deep evergreen actions, generous pauses, and humane copy keep the interface calm without making important decisions vague.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, low-contrast surfaces anchored by a deep evergreen action color.
Editorial serif headlines paired with a practical sans-serif interface voice.
Quiet borders, restrained depth, and generous vertical rhythm.
Direct state labels and recovery-oriented error copy.

rules.name: The Deliberate Green Rule
rules.body: Reserve evergreen for actions, focus, and meaningful state—not decoration.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Newsreader carries reflection and orientation; DM Sans carries every action and detail.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Persistent cards use border or tone; shadows indicate elevation or interaction.

dos: Do make the safest useful next action obvious within the first scan.
Do use warm surfaces and whitespace to separate content before adding decoration.
Do write control labels that state the outcome.
Do provide loading, empty, error, disabled, and recovery states.
donts: Don't use raw bright colors when an established semantic token exists.
Don't blur the distinction between professional support and emergency care.
Don't hide important fields behind icon-only controls without accessible labels.
Don't invent practitioner claims, verification, availability, or imagery.
